newsitem.title: UK: Seven-year gilts stay expensive in UK repo market.
newsitem.headline: Seven-year gilts stay expensive in UK repo market.

text.p: Eight percent gilts due 2003 continued to trade expensively on the gilt repo market on Friday, dealers said.
The seven year gilts traded around 4.5 percent overnight while general collateral rates hovered around 5.60 to 5.70 percent for most of the session.
The 6.0 percent gilts due 1999 and the 7.0 percents of 2001 were also trading on special, although not so spectacularly, traders said.
They added that an array of stocks on special in the repo market was a welcome development.
"In the first six months we had one special every couple of weeks on special. Now it's more like four or five," one repo trader said. "Things are hotting up."
But GC trade failed to take off. "The GC side is pretty dull," the trader said.
One week GC stood at 5.72/5.65 percent late on Friday, while one-month rates were at 5.69/5.64 percent.
UK money market rates softened on Friday having being squeezed for the previous two days, dealers said.
Overnight unsecured cash rates steadied at around 5-3/4, 5-5/8 percent having shot up to seven percent and higher on Thursday.
"We've had two tight days, but things have eased back a bit today," one money market dealer said. "Things are pretty lacklustre. The lack of a base rate cut didn't help."
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George met discuss monetary policy on Wednesday but left base rates unchanged at 5.75 percent.
Money market rates eased after seeing a moderate shortage, forecast at 800 million stg by the Bank of England, later revised up to 850 million.
On Thursday a 1.1 billion stg shortage, which went unfunded for most of the day, saw rates squeezed. Over the whole of Thursday, the Bank only managed to purchase bill worth 747 million stg.
One-week money market rates stood at 5-13/16, 5-11/16 percent late on Friday, while one month rates were 5-3/4, 5-11/16 percent.
